rationale: A wins because it has better editorial discipline: it refuses weak leaps and keeps the worker, consumer, investor, and benchmark angles structurally separate. Its best line, "Klarna won't distinguish layoffs from attrition, which is itself a newsworthy choice," is an actual accountability frame. B is useful, but it prints the mushy contrarian angle "The most-mocked category of enterprise AI might actually be working" and then worsens it with the fact error "two-thirds resolved." That is how a decent angle set walks itself into a correction.
gaps_in_A: "the equivalent of 700 people are gone" turns FTE-equivalent workload into people removed. The update does not prove 700 jobs disappeared.

"Consumer Advocates Are Questioning Whether an AI Should Decide Your Klarna Payment Dispute" overstates the fact pattern. The update says AI handles customer-service chats and advocates worry about disputes, not that AI decides disputes.

"Every Bank and Payments Company Now Has a Public Benchmark" is too sweeping. There is no supplied evidence that banks or payment companies view Klarna as a benchmark, or that the methodology is comparable.
"Before this, AI-in-customer-service claims were largely vendor-produced" is outside the supplied facts. Source it or cut it.
gaps_in_B: "two-thirds resolved" is a material fact error. The update says the assistant handles two-thirds of chats, not that it resolves two-thirds correctly.

"The most-mocked category of enterprise AI might actually be working" rests on an unsupported industry-reputation claim and a benefit claim the update cannot carry without satisfaction or complaint data.

"Klarna won't say how many of the jobs it cut were actually replaced by AI" implies confirmed job cuts and AI replacement. The update says headcount fell, partly through attrition, and Klarna will not break down roles cut versus left unfilled.

"five distinct, journalist-ready shapes exist" overstates readiness. The consumer and contrarian angles still need named advocates, incidents, escalation details, or CSAT data before reporter matching.
